deploy.after: Set `ADE_GENRES`, `ADE_ARTISTS` and `ADE_LATE_NIGHT` in the Edge agent's environment to configure the taste profile. Nothing leaves the host: no model is called anywhere in this pipeline. Add a selector with `match_labels` to pin the job to specific nodes.
deploy.intro: Pipelines here are deployed through Expanso Cloud and run by the Edge agent on your node. Credentials come from the environment, never from flags.
deploy.title: Deploy through Expanso Cloud

deploy.intro: The input listens on 127.0.0.1:8080 unless `INGEST_ADDRESS` says otherwise. Put TLS and authentication in front of it before it accepts traffic from another host. Each queue is a JSONL file under the agent's working directory; to deliver somewhere else, replace that queue's file output with the output your system needs. The decision logic upstream does not change.
deploy.title: Where it listens and where it writes

lede: Twenty-nine real Amsterdam Dance Event 2026 parties go in; three ranked lists come out. Expanso enriches each event (epoch times, weekday, time slot, lineup size), scores it against your taste with deterministic rules, and routes it to must-see, worth-it, or pass. No model is called anywhere in the path — this is the deterministic substrate the other examples pair with Jev.

run.after: The case prints pass or FAIL with the queues it wrote.
run.intro: The fixture runner deploys the pipeline exactly as shipped to a local Edge agent, posts every line of the input, and compares what the pipeline wrote with the expected output. It needs expanso-edge, expanso-cli and uv, and no Expanso Cloud credentials.
run.title: Run it with no account

run.after: Replace REPO with the path to your clone. Set `ADE_GENRES`, `ADE_ARTISTS` and `ADE_LATE_NIGHT` in the agent's environment before deploying to score with your own taste.
commands:
while read -r line; do \
  curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/events -d "$line"; \
done < REPO/demos/12-ade-schedule/input.jsonl
run.intro: The same thing without the runner. The pipeline writes `./data` in the agent's working directory, so start the agent in a scratch directory.
run.title: Run it by hand

stages.text: The input already parses JSON bodies. This stage only parses a body that arrives as a string, so both shapes become the same object before anything else touches it.
stages.title: Parse the body

stages.text: Turns the published schedule into epoch times and derived fields: duration in hours (after-midnight and multi-day events handled via end_day_offset), the weekday, the start hour, a morning/afternoon/evening/late-night time slot, and the lineup size. Everything downstream reads these.
stages.title: Enrich the event

stages.text: Deterministic preference rules, fully visible: genre match +40, artist match +30, live set +15, evening start +10, marathon session +5, late-night start -15 unless opted in. Taste comes from ADE_GENRES, ADE_ARTISTS and ADE_LATE_NIGHT in the agent's environment. Every point is explained in match_reasons.
stages.title: Score against your taste

stages.text: One cascade on the score: 70 or more is must-see, 40 or more is worth-it, everything else is pass. Change the profile and the whole schedule re-routes on the next run.
stages.title: Decide the tier

stages.text: A switch sends the record to one queue file by its tier. Each queue is a JSONL file under data/ade-schedule-builder/ so you can read exactly what landed. In production these files become real sinks: a calendar API, a Slack webhook, a mobile push.
stages.title: Write to a queue
